claim: REQ-506's reroute mechanism does not restrict its reroute target to a market-risk-free (risk:"safe") slot, directly contradicting the doctrine's own explicit promise in behavioral-spec.md §0: "Money-safety is preserved: 'always act' never means forcing a losing trade past a cap — when one skill (e.g. SOL) has no edge, the router routes to a market-risk-free skill (e.g. take a gig, post a clip) instead." As literally specified, REQ-506's reroute filter is `buildAlwaysActToolDefinitions(menuSlots.filter(x => x !== s))` — it removes ONLY the just-picked slot `s` from the enum and leaves every OTHER always-act-menu slot eligible, including other capital-risking (risk:"capital") slots such as hl_trade, token_launch, yield (new-deposit), earn/sol-trade, and earn/polymarket-trade, whenever the instance's balance is at/above BOOTSTRAP_RESERVE_USDC (REQ-503's carve-out only filters below-reserve, not above). Concretely: sol-trade's own baseline strategy (skills/earn/sol-trade/run.sh:54-66, 'if the signal is neutral/weak, DO NOT trade this session ... otherwise WAIT') explicitly instructs the agent to legitimately WAIT with no swap when there is no edge -- earning-health.py's own docstring (lines 18-22) calls this WAIT a 'real, legitimate decision' that 'must NEVER be flagged.' Under REQ-506 as written, that exact legitimate WAIT (earnLine===null) triggers a same-wake reroute whose tool schema STILL offers hl_trade / token_launch / earn/polymarket-trade (all capital-risking) as valid picks, with no sleep/idle escape this time (REQ-504). This is a NEW, feature-introduced money risk that did not exist before this feature: previously a legitimate 'no edge' WAIT ended the wake with zero further capital-risking attempts; after this feature, always-act's own reroute mechanism can pressure the model into a SECOND capital-risking action within the same wake specifically because REQ-508's escalation path is framed as 'RARE' and something to avoid, and the reroute enum offers no risk-tier restriction to prevent it.
evidence: behavioral-spec.md:10-12 (doctrine promise: "routes to a market-risk-free skill ... instead") vs REQ-506's EARS clause (behavioral-spec.md:261-278, esp. the literal filter `buildAlwaysActToolDefinitions(menuSlots.filter(x => x !== s))` at line 274) which has no risk-tag/safe-only restriction; cross-checked against real code: skills/registry.json:115-157 (yield/hl_trade/token_launch/earn/sol-trade/earn/polymarket-trade all `risk:"capital"`, `status:"live"`); skills/earn/sol-trade/run.sh:54-66 (baseline prompt explicitly instructs a legitimate no-trade WAIT); skills/self/earning-health.py:18-22 (docstring: a live-pass WAIT 'must NEVER be flagged' as unhealthy) — confirming the WAIT this reroute fires on is doctrine-sanctioned agent judgment, not a malfunction, yet REQ-506 forces the wake toward a further capital-risking attempt instead of doctrine's promised 'market-risk-free' alternative.
required_fix: REQ-506's reroute target MUST be restricted to (or at minimum default-preferenced toward) risk:"safe" / alwaysAvailable slots, mirroring the doctrine's own "routes to a market-risk-free skill instead" language -- e.g. `buildAlwaysActToolDefinitions(menuSlots.filter(x => x !== s && riskTagOf(x) === 'safe'))`, falling back to the full non-safe-filtered exclusion only when zero safe slots remain in the menu (an edge case that itself needs an explicit EARS clause + acceptance criteria, since REQ-503/REQ-502's own framing claims a safe slot is 'never filtered out by balance' and is the common-case expectation). Add a corresponding PROP (e.g. PROP-506e) asserting the reroute enum never contains a risk:"capital" slot unless the safe-slot pool is provably empty, plus an explicit money-safety acceptance test for the sol-trade-legitimate-WAIT -> reroute-to-hl_trade scenario shown above.
